assumptions: The feature flag is treated as the cause on the strength of timing and error-signature correlation alone; no one disabled it to confirm, so the diagnosis is unverified.

The alternative explanation — a pre-existing divide-by-zero defect in shipped code that the flag ramp merely exposed — was set aside because no deployment appears in the change log read, not because it was ruled out. Operationally the two stories imply the same immediate fix (turn the flag off) but different follow-up.

The incident's recorded end time coincides exactly with escalation to a human. It should be read as 'automation stopped working on this', not 'errors ceased'. Recovery time and total customer impact are therefore unknown from this record.
The 0–4% UpstreamTimeout errors present throughout the pre-incident window are assumed to be unrelated background noise from payment authorization, not part of this incident.
The log excerpt covering 13:40–13:52 appears three times in the record; it was treated as one reading of the same window, not as three separate observations.
input.executive_summary: On 12 September 2026, a newly switched-on feature on the online shop broke the account page for a large share of the customers who loaded it. The failures began at about 13:47 UTC, when the feature was turned on for nearly all traffic, and were still occurring at 13:52 when the alert fired. Customers hitting the account page saw an error instead of the page; other parts of the shop were not implicated in the evidence reviewed. The automated responder investigated, reached the same conclusion three times over roughly two minutes — that the newly enabled feature was at fault — but every proposed remedy was blocked because none of them was a reversible action the system is permitted to take on its own. It therefore changed nothing and handed the incident to a human at 13:54 UTC. The recorded end time is the moment of that handover, not a confirmed recovery: nothing in the evidence shows the feature being turned off or the errors stopping, so the true customer-facing duration may be longer than the alert window suggests.
input.root_cause: The `monthly-spend-feature` flag on io-shop was flipped from off to on at 13:47 (logs show a partial evaluation split at 13:47, fully on from 13:48), and the code path it enables raises ZeroDivisionError while rendering the account page — the logged per-minute error rate on that page jumped from the usual 0–4% to the high-20s/mid-30s in the same minute, and the dominant error signature switched from sporadic UpstreamTimeout to ZeroDivisionError. This is a timing-and-signature correlation only: the flag was never turned back off during the incident, so the causal link was never confirmed by test. A second story (a latent divide-by-zero defect in already-deployed code that the flag merely exposed) is not distinguishable from the first on the evidence read, since no deployment appears in the change log for the preceding week.
